data.narrative:
Blue Water Autonomy, founded by Rylan Hamilton and Austin Gray, is a Series A-stage defense and security company that has raised $64M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms, including four same-stage defense and security companies (Stark Defence at $4.0B, Castelion at $1.0B, Singularity at $400M, and NODA AI at $125M).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $64M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies $128M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $700M, with a range spanning $125M to $4.0B. This wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity within early-stage defense tech valuations.

Triangulation of both methods produces a valuation range of $109M (low) to $805M (high), with a median point of $414M. The substantial gap between the stage-progression floor and peer median reflects uncertainty about whether Blue Water Autonomy will command a premium or discount to peer valuations. Key uncertainties include revenue traction relative to comparables, customer concentration risk, and technology differentiation within a sector showing wide valuation variance.
